clue.text: Very English place seeing off a large expedition

definitions.note: in the old sense of speed or promptness

indicators.note: to see something off is to get rid of it, so the following letters are dropped

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for English
a locality is a place or district
A as written, plus L, the abbreviation for large, both to be removed

explanation.surface: A grand English location sends off a big expedition party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey, but here it has its older sense of speed, as in 'with all expedition'.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or haste, and velocity is speed.

clue.text: Set up to keep brain active and lively

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: a TV set, the television

indicators.note: active letters are on the move, so they get rearranged

parts.note: the letters of brain rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets their mind sharp and lively by setting it up properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is a noun here, short for TV set; turned upwards it becomes VT, which then holds the jumbled BRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrant and lively are synonyms, both describing something full of energy.

clue.text: Boy removing nothing from large quantity

indicators.note: removing means taking a letter out of the following word

parts.note: a load is a large amount
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A boy takes nothing out of a big heap.
explanation.walkthrough: LOAD loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is a boy or young man, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Right-winger supporting obscurity, not rocking the boat

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative
to be for something is to support it
mist obscures the view

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician backing vagueness who never stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is short for a Conservative, the British right-wing party.
explanation.definitionFit: A conformist goes along with accepted norms, so does not make waves or upset the status quo.

clue.text: Propose bill supported by Liberal European

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Putting forward a parliamentary bill with Liberal and European backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supported by' puts TAB above L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To table a motion is, in British usage, to put it forward for discussion.

clue.text: Area of intellectual activity affected our group

parts.note: camp means affected or theatrical in manner
us refers to our group

explanation.surface: A field of thinking that has influenced our team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like a verb meaning influenced, but it is the adjective, as in an affected manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A university campus is the grounds where academic study and research go on.

clue.text: Religious symbol carried by Khan repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the name is written out twice, one copy after the other
what is carried by something rides inside it, so the outer letters of the doubled name fall away

parts.note: the name taken as written, twice over, with the answer straddling the join

explanation.surface: A sacred emblem worn again and again by a man named Khan.
explanation.walkthrough: Writing the name twice gives KHANKHAN, and the answer sits in the middle, carried by the doubled name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is an ancient Egyptian cross with a loop, a symbol of life.

clue.text: Pay lone pair to rehash instrument from the 1920s?

indicators.note: to rehash is to rework old material into a new form

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Paying a solitary couple to rework some old music.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: these self-playing pianos were at their peak in the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola or self-playing piano was hugely popular in homes during the 1920s, so it typifies that decade.

clue.text: Was ahead after several games, needing extra time? Agreed

indicators.note: after places the phrase before it later, so the leading piece is sent second

parts.note: in tennis a set is made of several games
an extra T, the abbreviation for time
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A player was in front after a long match that needed extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a set is a group of games, which is how 'several games' gives its piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Settled means decided or agreed upon, as in a settled matter.

clue.text: Herbal remedy: always fine with small quantity about

indicators.note: about means around, so one part goes round the others

parts.note: a few is a small number
ever means always
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A herbal cure is always fine in small doses.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine; the always-and-fine pair goes inside the small quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverfew is a daisy-like plant traditionally taken to relieve headaches and fevers.

clue.text: Backing of French in group quickly pursuing holiday place to stay

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this part comes after the earlier one
in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: de is French for of
a break is a short holiday
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A rush to leave a group, somewhere to stay on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quickly pursuing holiday' means the word for quickly comes after the word for holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed and breakfast is a guesthouse offering overnight lodging, a place to stay.

clue.text: Fellows back in area — remote, rocky — getting measure of wind

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the backwards direction
something rocky is unsteady, so its letters are shaken up

parts.note: fellows are men
the letters of remote rearranged

explanation.surface: Men far out in rugged, remote terrain measure the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In area' means placed within the area clue's letters, here after the A; NEM then jumbled REMOTE follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An anemometer is the instrument that gauges wind speed, so it is a measure of wind.

clue.text: Condition accepted by each bloke in property job

definitions.note: describes the person doing the job

indicators.note: what is accepted by something is taken inside it

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
a state is a condition
a gent is a man or bloke

explanation.surface: Each man working in property has accepted the terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a person by their trade: one who works in property.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent is the British term for a realtor, someone who works in buying and selling property.

clue.text: Went over cruel hill
Historic garment design getting no initial surprised reaction

indicators.note: no initial means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times
a make is a design or brand

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned garment design that has lost its first letter.
explanation.walkthrough: MAKE loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: A double take is a delayed second look of surprise at something just noticed.

clue.text: What stand-up comedian may do, having a symbolic impact

wordplay.note: a stand-up carries a microphone around the stage

explanation.surface: A comedian's act has a deeper symbolic effect.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, TOTE MIC: to tote is to carry, and a mic is a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Totemic means emblematic, having the power of a totem, an object that stands for something larger.

clue.text: Injured person's left for time without adequate attention?

indicators.note: one letter put in place of another, as one thing exchanged for another

parts.note: a casualty is someone hurt in an accident
L is the abbreviation for left
T is the abbreviation for time, the letter replaced

explanation.surface: A wounded patient has been left for ages without proper care.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Injured person' is 'has': the T of CASUALTY has L put in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something casually means doing it offhandedly, with little care or thought.

clue.text: Pay for accommodation for thief

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
a pad is slang for a home or flat

explanation.surface: Settling the bill for a place to stay, or for a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was a highwayman on foot, a robber who preyed on travellers in earlier centuries.

clue.text: Sculptors possibly recalled pose in pieces lacking head

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
lacking a head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: parts are pieces

indicators.note: recalled suggests being called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: Sculptors look back at a model's pose broken into fragments without a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pose' here is what a model does for a painter, not a noun for a stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculptors are one kind of artist, so the plural is defined by example, signalled by 'possibly'.

clue.text: Charged, but doomed to lose power ultimately

indicators.note: to lose something is to remove a letter

parts.note: accursed means doomed or under a curse

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of a word

parts.note: the end of power

explanation.surface: Charged, but a defendant facing doom drops their strength in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: ACCURSED drops R.
explanation.definitionFit: The accused is the person formally charged with a crime, so accused means charged.

clue.text: We will need security about source of messages here

definitions.text: We will need security about source of messages here

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means around, wrapping one piece round the other

parts.note: bail is money given as security for release

indicators.note: the source of something is its starting point, so the first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of messages

explanation.surface: We need security covering where our messages come from.
explanation.walkthrough: Bail is money lodged as security for a prisoner's release. The whole clue also reads as a description of the answer: a secure place we keep messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Webmail is email read through a browser, an online inbox that needs a password to protect it.

clue.text: Italian food — the way to circumvent depression

indicators.note: to circumvent is literally to go around something

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
a sag is a dip or depression

explanation.surface: Italian comfort food is the cure for feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood, but here it is a dip in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is the baked Italian dish of layered pasta sheets, sauce and filling.

clue.text: Bring round article held by apple grower

indicators.note: what is held by something is enclosed within it

parts.note: Richard Cox raised the Cox's Orange Pippin apple
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An orchard keeper turns a written piece over in his hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Cox's Orange Pippin is a classic English eating apple, named after its grower.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone is to persuade them gently, to bring them round to your view.

clue.text: Ghastly party securing state in California, America

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly inside
in puts the combined piece inside another

parts.note: a do is a party
to aver is to state firmly
US for United States

explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a US state but is the verb meaning declare; California and America together wrap the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadaverous means corpse-like, pale and gaunt, so it describes a ghastly look.

clue.text: Literary lion using a lot of dodgy language?

indicators.note: a lot of something is most of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
slang is informal, not quite respectable language

explanation.surface: A famous storybook lion who talks in a disreputable way.
explanation.walkthrough: SLANG drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslan is the great lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia books.

clue.text: Image of sun is captured in revolutionary data storage medium

indicators.note: captured in means held inside
something revolutionary turns around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the two-letter short form for the shiny optical format used for music and data
taken as written

explanation.surface: A picture of the sun stored on a turning computer disk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Data storage medium' looks like the definition, since the answer is one; it is CD in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun appears in the sky, and in pictures, as a round flat disc.

clue.text: Place is buzzing: politician's beginning significant dodgy argument

indicators.note: a buzzing place is all bustle, so its letters are stirred up

parts.note: the letters of place and is rearranged

parts.note: the opening letter of politician
leading means principal or significant

explanation.surface: A lively venue where a politician's first important speech is suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Special pleading is a fallacious argument that cites only the facts favourable to one side.

clue.text: Hotel popular around November

indicators.note: around means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
N is November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel is in demand around November.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a small hotel or pub offering lodging.

clue.text: Separate account in heartless conclusion

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: death is the end of life
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: An unfeeling ending recorded separately in the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes only the single central letter of the five-letter word for conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach is to separate one thing from another.

clue.text: Seabird captured in cold season not showing wings: one's caged as a precaution

indicators.note: captured in means held inside
the wings of a word are its outer letters, here both dropped

parts.note: winter is the cold season
the erne is the sea eagle

explanation.surface: A seabird trapped through a wingless winter is caged for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings' suggests a bird, but it means the outer letters of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is someone confined, as in wartime, as a security precaution rather than for a crime.
